page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 40 dedicated physical cores and 40 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.4 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates solid compute capabilities, achieving a stress-ng single-core performance score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56. Its memory subsystem delivers a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2132.58 GB/sec, which drops to 105.52 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 36.66 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which assist in vector calculations and cryptography tasks, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 35311.94 and an encryption score of 17670.65.

The instance is well-suited for compute-intensive workloads that require high clock speeds and dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand massive memory footprints or local SSD storage. It performs efficiently in database operations, registering 13891.08 operations on Passmark and handling 34.66 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. It also supports light machine learning tasks, processing 57.07 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B LLM model. However, the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration limits its utility for large-scale deep learning or high-speed local data caching.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 40 dedicated vCPUs and 40 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor, it includes 96.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 2.4 GB per core density, with no local storage or GPU resources. The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark results indicate strong compute performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 38381.56 and a Passmark CPU score of 34144.54. It supports AVX-512 instruction sets, making it highly capable for cryptography, vector calculations, and database operations, where it achieves 34.66 million Redis SET operations per second. This hardware profile is optimized for high-performance web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and compute-heavy enterprise applications that do not require local storage.
